D8 equalisation: a qualifying race one fleet never sailed does not count for anyone

ILCA 7 2024 — World Championship, Adelaide AUS (Addendum A2.8) · F1 · D8 · SI (reference-docs:events/ilca7-worlds-2024/SI-Amendment-1.pdf) · results (reference-docs:events/ilca7-worlds-2024/results-sailwave.html)

2 qualifying fleets · → Gold/Silver · discards: 1 discard from race 4.
A qualifying race only counts once every fleet has completed it: "A
qualifying series race will not count until all qualifying series fleets have
completed that race" (ILCA SI 7.7), and end-of-qualifying, ILCA abandons the
surplus so every boat has equal counts (Addendum A2.8). Here Yellow sailed a
second qualifying race that Blue never did, so that logical race is
incomplete and counts for nobody — Yellow's Q2 scores are recorded but
struck from the total. The standings rest on Q1 alone.

This is the common case of the equalisation rule, and it is the whole of
what `equalization: abandon-extra-races` does. The per-boat refinement —
Appendix LE 20.4(a) / 2026 ILCA SI 18.3, where a boat still left holding
more scores than the rest drops her most recent — composes on top of this
gate rather than replacing it, and is selected with
`equalization: exclude-extra-scores`. It is covered by unit test rather
than fixture: with well-formed ceremony data the gate already equalises
everyone, so the clause only bites on states an assignment override can
reach. `expected` verified against the engine: y1/y2/y3 net counts Q1 only
(net 1/2/3), not Q1+Q2.
